instruction: State the results of the 2022 Super Bowl, including the points scored.

metadata.explanation: Task variation for 2022 Super Bowl scores with question-style phrasing for natural language diversity. Same complexity and interaction pattern as original - user navigates from NFL.com to the specific year's Super Bowl page. The evaluator confirms the active tab URL matches the expected 2022 Super Bowl scores page (post4). No new functions needed - reuses existing Chrome evaluation infrastructure.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies navigation to the 2022 Super Bowl scores page at https://www.nfl.com/scores/2022/post4
Getter (active_url_from_accessTree) can successfully extract the active tab URL from accessibility tree
Metric (is_expected_active_tab) correctly compares the active URL with expected URL using compare_urls() function
Expected URL is semantically correct - post4 corresponds to Super Bowl LVI in 2022
Data flow is correct: getter extracts URL -> metric compares with expected URL

Minor semantic issue: instruction is phrased as a question ('What were the scores...?') implying information extraction, but evaluator only verifies navigation to the page, not comprehension of the scores
However, this appears to be a Mind2Web navigation task where the goal is page navigation rather than information extraction, so the evaluator aligns with the actual task intent
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider rephrasing instruction to 'Navigate to the 2022 Super Bowl scores page' to better match what the evaluator verifies
Alternatively, if the instruction should verify that scores are actually found, add a getter to extract score information from the page content and verify specific score values
